extracted.intended_audience: children's book illustrators, publishers, editors, and awards judges (ALSC/Caldecott community)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guidance for judging the most distinguished American picture book for children (Caldecott Medal), focused on the quality and role of the illustrations and their relationship to text and the child audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of Execution in the Artistic Technique Employed
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever medium or technique the illustrator uses (watercolor, collage, digital, mixed media), it must be executed at a high level of craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical mastery and control of the chosen medium; look for sophistication, consistency, and intentionality in technique regardless of whether it is traditional or experimental. Poorly executed media, even if conceptually interesting, will undermine distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of Pictorial Interpretation of Story, Theme, or Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations must interpret — not merely accompany — the text. They should advance, deepen, or counterpoint the story's meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how pictures add meaning beyond the words: whether they reveal subtext, extend themes, provide new perspectives, or offer counterpoint. Illustrations that only replicate surface text without contributing interpretation are weaker under this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of Style of Illustration to Story, Theme, or Concept
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider fit between pictorial style and the book’s content and tone. A mismatch (e.g., a horror story illustrated like a baby book or vice versa) indicates a failure of appropriateness. Style should support and enhance the story’s intent and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of Plot, Theme, Characters, Setting, Mood, or Information through the Pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictures must carry narrative weight. They should communicate plot beats, evoke mood, characterize figures, establish place, or transmit information — not merely decorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether illustrations clearly convey narrative elements and emotional tone, making the story comprehensible and resonant through images alone or in interaction with text. Look for sequencing, visual storytelling choices, and how images handle exposition or pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of Presentation in Recognition of a Child Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be for children — visually navigable, age-appropriate, inviting. Adults' aesthetic admiration alone does not qualify a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine suitability for children in layout, pacing, clarity, and design: readability of images at appropriate scale, visual entry points, and overall accessibility to the intended child age range. A book primarily appealing only to adult aesthetics may fail this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Text, Design, Typography, and Overall Book Object as They Affect Illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Text, design, typography, and overall book object may be considered as they affect the effectiveness of the illustrations, but the primary judgment is on the pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While illustrations are primary, evaluate how design choices (type, layout, integration of text and image, production qualities) support or detract from the pictorial achievement. Effective integration of text and image as a unified object strengthens the book’s distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Recipient and Integration of Text and Image
rubrics_metrics.description: The award goes to the illustrator, but text-illustration integration is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that the Caldecott recognizes the illustrator’s achievement; however, judges should assess collaborative effectiveness where text and image interact. Strong illustration work within a well-integrated book is favored, but the primary credit is for pictorial accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Evaluation Checklist (Implications for a Picture-Book Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture book can be evaluated on technical execution of the chosen medium; how much the pictures interpret (not just illustrate); fit between pictorial style and story; the narrative weight pictures carry; whether the book truly addresses children; integration of text and image as a unified object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist to operationalize the five core criteria: score technical craft, interpretive contribution, stylistic appropriateness, narrative clarity/weight, child-centered presentation, and the effectiveness of text-image integration. Each item reflects the corresponding core criterion and can be used for comparative ranking.
